entries.title: Web browsers take center stage
entries.quote: 2005 will see much activity around the web browser. There will be more competition, more choice and more functionality.
entries.subject: Web browsers
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Fuel cells debut
entries.quote: 2005 will see the first commercial launch of ethanol-based fuel cells, both as standalone products and as the integrated power source for leading-edge consumer products.
entries.subject: Fuel cells for portable devices
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Super small technology. Huge returns
entries.quote: Nanotechnology – one of the most talked about but least understood technologies of the 21st century – will become increasingly mainstream in 2005.
entries.subject: Nanotechnology
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Connected devices under siege
entries.quote: Massive growth in the number of connected devices – from PCs and mobile phones to digital music players and gaming consoles – will cause a corresponding leap in electronic viruses and other malicious attacks.
entries.subject: Malware
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: The robot invasion
entries.quote: After decades in science fiction, in 2005 robots will increasingly become an accepted part of our daily lives.
entries.subject: Household robots
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Mesh networks hit the streets
entries.quote: By the end of 2005, wireless mesh networks will have appeared in several major urban centers throughout Northern Europe, the United States and Asia.
entries.subject: Mesh networking
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Flat screen frenzy
entries.quote: In 2005, consumers will spend billions of dollars on liquid crystal displays (LCDs) and plasma flat panel screens, fueling strong market growth – particularly for large format devices such as televisions and computer monitors.
entries.metric: consumer spend on flat panel screens
entries.subject: Flat-panel displays
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Digital crime runs rampant
entries.quote: 2005 will see a rapid increase in electronic forms of identification, as governments around the world move to replace paper-based IDs with digital products. ... yet identify theft and other digital crimes will continue to wreak havoc.
entries.subject: Digital identity and cybercrime
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005). Second sentence from the report's summary.

entries.title: The space race moves into the private sector
entries.quote: First, there is likely to be an acceleration of the shift from the public to private sector, with public space agencies under increasing pressure to open up the market for launch vehicles and services.
entries.subject: Commercial spaceflight
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005).

entries.title: Quantum computing gets closer to reality
entries.quote: Quantum computers, which are expected to be many orders of magnitude faster than today's fastest supercomputers, will take a few important steps closer to commercial reality.
entries.subject: Quantum computing
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the full Deloitte Technology report (2 February 2005). Quote from the report's summary.

entries.title: Music downloading gets respectable
entries.quote: 2005 will see rapid growth in legal music downloads over the internet. Illegal downloading will most likely still dominate, but legal sites will significantly increase their share.
entries.subject: Legal music downloads
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: The mass audience becomes a mass of audiences
entries.quote: In 2005, the long-standing business model for broadcast television – the network model – is likely to be increasingly replaced by a more segmented, customer-centric approach.
entries.subject: Broadcast TV audience fragmentation
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Advertising gets embedded
entries.quote: During the course of the year, more advanced forms of embedded advertisement will appear in video games, software (particularly freeware), web browsers and even active desktops on mobile phones.
entries.subject: In-game and embedded advertising
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Convergence pays off – but only for a few
entries.quote: Convergence will certainly remain a hotly debated topic; however, it is only likely to deliver strong returns for a handful of media companies.
entries.subject: Media convergence
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Games and movies: a blockbuster combination
entries.quote: Blockbuster movies will increasingly be developed in tandem with best-selling games, using the same characters, the same narrative threads, the same look and feel
entries.subject: Game and film convergence
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Mixed returns from internet publishing
entries.quote: Many newspaper publishers will probably generate only modestly rising returns from their on-line activities.
entries.subject: Online newspaper revenue
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Also: niche journals likely to expand subscription-based electronic versions.

entries.title: Content for the masses, by the masses
entries.quote: Although such activities are unlikely to cause a noticeable drop in revenue for traditional media companies, they will increasingly compete for the public's time and attention
entries.subject: Blogs and user-generated content
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. 'Such activities' are blogs and wikis.

entries.title: Digital terrestrial TV takes off
entries.quote: Digital terrestrial television (DTTV) is currently being launched in a number of countries, and 2005 will see a substantial increase in the number and size of deployments.
entries.subject: Digital terrestrial television
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Knock-offs get knocked out
entries.quote: In 2005, the media industry will launch its most sustained and successful attack so far on piracy and copyright theft.
entries.subject: Media piracy enforcement
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Simple phone content sells best
entries.quote: By the end of 2005, there will likely be two billion mobile subscriptions.
entries.subject: Mobile subscriptions
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Chapter's main claim is that simple personalization content (ringtones, wallpapers) outsells mobile TV and complex services.

entries.title: Small talk by billions adds up to big revenue
entries.quote: By the end of 2005, there will be nearly 2 billion cellular mobile subscriptions worldwide.
entries.subject: Mobile subscriptions
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Also: voice typically more than 80 percent of total revenue.

entries.title: 3G emerges from the shadows
entries.quote: 2005 will see dozens of 3G networks go live. Initial consumer interest and adoption may well be low, but by year-end the situation should improve markedly in many countries.
entries.subject: 3G mobile networks
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Mobile penetration surpasses 100 percent
entries.quote: Mobile penetration in excess of 100 percent, will become reality in a growing number of markets in 2005.
entries.subject: Mobile penetration
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Simplicity sells
entries.quote: The most compelling and lucrative mobile content will continue to revolve around phone personalization.
entries.subject: Mobile content
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Segmentation delivers higher margins
entries.quote: In 2005, operators will likely take a more scientific approach to segmentation and marketing.
entries.subject: Mobile operator segmentation
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Messaging is critical to success
entries.quote: Mobile e-mail will grow very rapidly in both the personal and enterprise markets, and text messaging will continue to account for up to 20 percent of operator revenue.
entries.metric: text messaging share of operator revenue
entries.subject: Mobile messaging
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Convergence blows hot and cold
entries.quote: Experiments with TV and radio on mobile phones will tend to generate little value, as quality, cost and relevance hinder adoption.
entries.subject: Mobile TV
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Operators spread their bets too thin
entries.quote: Many mobile and fixed operators will continue to adopt new wireless technologies in rapid succession.
entries.subject: Operator technology investment
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. The report names WiFi hotspots, HSDPA, DAB, DVB-H and WiMAX.

entries.title: WiFi sizzles but hotspots remain cold
entries.quote: The market for private WiFi installations will continue to skyrocket.
entries.subject: Wi-Fi
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Also: deployment of public WiFi hotspots will probably continue to outpace usage.

entries.title: RFID: The giant awakens
entries.quote: By the end of the year, billions of RFID tags are expected to have been commissioned.
entries.subject: RFID
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: PSTN fights to keep its lead
entries.quote: In 2005, the vast majority of voice calls will still originate and terminate on the PSTN (Public Switched Telephony Network).
entries.subject: Fixed-line voice
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: VoIP accelerates but remains niche and unprofitable
entries.quote: VoIP will remain a niche product in 2005, but its importance to the global voice market will grow substantially.
entries.subject: VoIP
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Low-cost operators get stronger
entries.quote: In 2005, the performance of low-cost telecom operators will most likely become increasingly impressive and threatening.
entries.subject: Low-cost telecom operators
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Robust growth but falling profitability for broadband
entries.quote: Although broadband penetration will continue to grow, profitability will generally decline. In many countries, broadband providers will celebrate the fact that broadband connections finally outnumber dial-up
entries.subject: Broadband adoption
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Technology developments drive demand for fixed-line bandwidth
entries.quote: Overall demand for fixed-line bandwidth will grow steadily throughout 2005, and there are strong indications this growth will continue until at least 2010.
entries.subject: Fixed-line bandwidth demand
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: WiMAX makes headlines but not money
entries.quote: WiMAX – a wireless data standard also known as 802.16, and apparent heir to WiFi (802.11) – is likely to remain on trial in 2005.
entries.subject: WiMAX
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Selective convergence pays dividends
entries.quote: In 2005, fixed-line operators can expect to see an increasing number of new opportunities to generate revenue from convergence
entries.subject: Fixed-line convergence services
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. The report lists broadband games, electronic magazine subscriptions and consumer video over IP.

entries.title: Fixed and mobile diverge to preserve value
entries.quote: In 2005, several operators will launch converged telephone services that feature fixed line pricing within buildings and mobile pricing when outdoors
entries.subject: Fixed-mobile convergence
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Also: initial rate of adoption likely to be limited.

entries.title: WiFi sizzles but hotspots stay cold
entries.quote: Although fee-based hotspots will struggle, global use of WiFi will continue to grow
entries.subject: Wi-Fi
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Fiber goes home
entries.quote: Fiber to the home (FTTH) – a revolutionary technology long regarded by fixed operators as their most potent weapon – is expected to take a huge leap forward in 2005.
entries.subject: Fiber to the home
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

notes: 4th edition by count from 2002. 'TMT Trends: Predictions, 2005 - A focus on the technology sector'; ten predictions stated in the foreword, all ten captured. Computerworld (20 January 2005) calls it 'the company's first publication of technological predictions', which fits Deloitte's statement that the series began in 2001 with ten predictions about mobile telephony. None of the ten headlines carries a number. Internet Archive retry (2026-10-02): the 2005 edition had four reports, not three: Technology, Media, Mobile and Wireless, and Wireline ('TMT Trends: Predictions, 2005 - A focus on the ... sector', each stating ten predictions, dated 14 January 2005; the Wireline copy read is dated 28 January 2005). Media, Mobile and Wireless and Wireline were read in full from deloitte.com/dtt/ copies on archive.org (entries 11 to 40); the Technology entries (1 to 10) stay as captured from Mondaq.
